Prevention: Public awareness and encouraging farmers to report outbreaks to
Ministries is a major initial step in prevention and control.
Avoid planting sorghum near water points as these birds like water areas.
Time the planting of sorghum so that it flowers at the same time as wild grasses (which are preferred by the birds).
Cover sorghum heads with cloth or weaved grass or leaf sheaths to protect them bird attack.
Monitoring: A flock of 2,000,000 birds can cause up to 50 tons of sorghum losses per attack.
However, the birds prefer seeds of wild grasses and only attack cereals when their preferred food is scarce.

Look for 10-15cm small, short-tailed birds with different amounts of black, yellow, pink, purplish or white feathers on the head and neck and different amounts of colouration on the belly among the moving in flocks.

Direct Control: Control of weaver birds is very difficult unless populations are small.
Put about 4-5 human dummies (scarecrows) per hectare to scare away small populations.
When larger bird flocks are around, scare birds by shouting, blasting, rattling with cans or throwing stones.
